"Role: Mobile Game Developer @COMMENT_BODY@ Touch UI Specialist
Tech Stack: HTML5 Canvas / Phaser.js (or Unity C#) - Targeted for Mobile Android Browsers @COMMENT_BODY@ WebView (No Keyboard or Mouse required).

Goal: Build a top-down, touch-optimized Android action/strategy game titled \"Fire Marshal: Touch Protocol\". The player controls a firefighter using virtual touch controls to select tools, place extinguishers, extinguish specific fire types, and draw touch-gesture evacuation routes around blast radius zones before launching a live fire drill simulation.

---

### 1. TOUCH CONTROL SCHEME @COMMENT_BODY@ ON-SCREEN UI (Android Native Feel)

No hardware keys (WASD, Mouse, Scroll Wheel) are used. Everything must operate via touch input:

#### A. Dual Virtual Touch Joysticks (GTA-Style Mobile Movement)
- Left Virtual D-Pad / Joystick (Bottom-Left Screen): Floating or fixed touch joystick to control 360-degree walking movement.
- Right Touch Aiming Zone (Right Half Screen): Dragging on the right side of the screen aims the firefighter's facing direction/hose nozzle in 360 degrees. Tapping/holding the \"FIRE / ACTION\" button sprays the nozzle.

#### B. On-Screen Touch Radial Wheels (Replacing Mouse Scroll Wheels)
- Left Extinguisher Radial Touch Button (Extinguisher Icon):
  - Tapping opens a semi-transparent circular wheel around the thumb with 4 selectable touch segments:
    - 🔴 Water (Class A - Trash/Wood)
    - 🔵 CO2 (Class C - Electrical)
    - 🟡 Dry Chem (Class B - Fuel)
    - ⚪ Wet Chem (Class K - Grease)
- Right Tool Radial Touch Button (Planning Tool Icon):
  - Tapping opens a radial menu for:
    - 🖌️ Route Painter Tool
    - 🧯 Wall Extinguisher Installer Tool
    - 🚧 Danger Zone Marker

---

### 2. PRE-DRILL PLANNING @COMMENT_BODY@ EXPLOSION DANGER ZONES

#### A. Touch Vector Route Painting
- When the Route Painter Tool is selected from the touch wheel, the player can touch and drag a finger across floor tiles to paint glowing green directional arrows connecting room doors to Exit Doors.
- Touch-to-Erase: Swiping over an existing route erases it.

#### B. Dynamic Blast Radius Intersection
- Volatile equipment (Transformers, Gas Tanks, Deep Fryers) projects pulsing red danger circles on the floor (e.g., 4-meter radius).
- Path Safety Validator:
  - The path system dynamically checks if painted green path vectors intersect any red blast radius.
  - If a path crosses a blast radius, that segment turns Flashing Red with a touch alert banner (\"UNSAFE ROUTE: EVACUEES AT EXPLOSION RISK\").
  - Civilian NPCs will refuse to use a route that crosses an unmitigated blast circle.

---

### 3. EXTINGUISHER SELECTION @COMMENT_BODY@ FIRE PHYSICS

- Fire Types @COMMENT_BODY@ Chemical Logic:
  - Class A (Combustibles): Water smothers quickly; CO2 has low effect.
  - Class C (Electrical Racks): CO2 smothers safely. Spraying Water causes an explosion and instant path failure.
  - Class K (Kitchen Grease): Wet Chem smothers safely. Spraying Water triggers an expanding fireball cone.
- Spray Mechanics: Pressing the on-screen \"SPRAY\" button emits 2D particle cones in the direction set by the right aim control.

---

### 4. GAME PHASES @COMMENT_BODY@ LOOP

1. Phase 1: Touch Preparation (2 Minutes)
   - Walk the Fire Marshal through the facility using the left joystick.
   - Use the radial menu to equip extinguishers and mount the correct types onto empty wall sockets near high-risk rooms.
   - Use the touch painter to draw safe evacuation lines around red explosion circles.
2. Phase 2: Live Drill Test
   - Tap the red \"START DRILL\" button at the top-right of the HUD.
   - Test fires break out. NPCs spawn and walk along painted routes. If all routes avoid explosion zones and correct extinguishers were placed/used, the facility achieves a 100% Safety Pass Score.

---

### 5. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Build a single-file or clean modular script containing:
1. Touch Input Handler:
   - Multitouch support (`touchstart`, `touchmove`, `touchend`) handling simultaneous left joystick movement and right aiming/spraying.
   - Touch drag detection for the green path painter tool.
2. Canvas Rendering Engine:
   - 2D grid/tilemap rendering with pixel-art or clean vector visuals optimized for 60 FPS on Android mobile GPUs.
3. Path Safety @COMMENT_BODY@ Polygon Intersection Algorithm:
   - Function `checkPathSafety(pathPoints, blastCircles)` that detects overlapping geometric bounds and updates visual path states.
4. UI HUD Layer:
   - Scalable touch buttons and touch-friendly radial menus anchored to screen corners.

Write clean, fully functional TypeScript or HTML5 JavaScript code implementing the touch joysticks, touch path-painting tool, radial menus, and blast-zone validation logic.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, touch-first Android browser game titled “Fire Marshal: Touch Protocol.”
- Repair and expand the existing game so spraying works throughout the drill, water supply depletes visibly, more levels and fire types are supported, and the danger tool works.

## Requirements
- Use HTML5 Canvas/JavaScript or TypeScript; no keyboard or mouse required.
- Support multitouch movement, aiming, spraying, radial equipment/tool menus, route painting/erasing, extinguisher installation, and danger-zone mitigation.
- Implement `checkPathSafety(pathPoints, blastCircles)` and render unsafe routes distinctly.
- Make the game mobile-friendly and playable; user requested no clarifying questions.
- Latest request: “The fire fighter cant shoot at all times while the drill is started, make it shoot whenever i press shoot water, also make a bar that manages the water that can deplete, also make more levels and all the fire types so that could be extinguished, also the danger tool doesnt work, repair all these”

## Decisions
- Single-file `index.html` Canvas game, no framework or external dependencies.
- Pointer Events are used for touch interaction.
- Water should be allowed to extinguish any fire type per latest request.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial Canvas facility scene, fire/hazard/equipment entities, exits, characters, HUD, touch controls, radial menus, route planning, and drill loop in `index.html`.
- Added `window.checkPathSafety`; unsafe routes render distinctly.
- Closed the missing JavaScript IIFE in `index.html`; script passes `node --check`.
- Made evacuation require a safe route that reaches an exit.
- Headless Chromium rendered the game at 430×932; screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/fire-marshal-final.jpg`.
- Adjusted small-screen aiming and HUD placement.

### Active
- Implement latest request: reliable spray while drill is live, depletable water bar, additional levels and fire types, and repair danger mitigation.
- Inspect and test touch controls and the complete drill loop after changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` spray, fire-type/equipment, level, danger-tool, and HUD logic.
2. Make spray activate continuously while held in live drills and make water extinguish all fire types; add a visible water meter that depletes and refills/reset appropriately.
3. Add multiple playable levels and corresponding fire types/hazards.
4. Repair danger-tool selection/activation and verify blast-zone mitigation updates route safety.
5. Run `node --check`, then test in Chromium and inspect an updated mobile screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; all requested repairs and expansion are centered here.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; existing workspace contains untracked files including `index.html`.
- Current `spray()` requires the equipment class to match the fire (`A`/water, `C`/CO₂, `K`/wet chemical, `B`/dry chemical), and damage is applied in small increments.
- Current code uses only one fixed level and three fires.
- Danger mitigation is toggled by tapping near a hazard only while `state.phase==='PREP'` and `state.tool==='danger'`; verify selection and hit-testing.
- Recent edits made `aim()` and `spray()` trigger `spray()` during updates, but this behavior has not been interactively tested.

## Objective
- Complete “Fire Marshal: Touch Protocol,” a playable touch-first browser game.
- Fix held spraying and water depletion, add fire types and levels, and repair the danger mitigation tool.

## Requirements
- Use HTML5 Canvas/JavaScript with touch-first controls; no keyboard or mouse required.
- Support movement, aiming, spraying, tool menus, route planning, extinguisher installation, and danger-zone mitigation.
- Render unsafe evacuation routes distinctly and expose `checkPathSafety(pathPoints, blastCircles)`.
- Latest request: “The fire fighter cant shoot at all times while the drill is started, make it shoot whenever i press shoot water, also make a bar that manages the water that can deplete, also make more levels and all the fire types so that could be extinguished, also the danger tool doesnt work, repair all these”

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation in a single `index.html` file with no framework or external dependencies.
- Water can extinguish all fire types; other equipment remains selectable.
- Progress to the next level after a successful drill; retry the current level after a failed drill.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented continuous spraying while the spray control is held during a live drill, with visible water depletion and a refill bonus for extinguishing fires.
- Added four levels with multiple fire types and per-level hazards.
- Improved danger-zone hit testing and made mitigated zones visibly distinct and safe for route checks.
- Added level, fire-count, and water-meter HUD updates; drill completion now reflects the current level’s fire count.
- `node --check /tmp/opencode/fire-marshal.js` passed after extracting the script from `index.html`.

### Active
- Test the updated touch gameplay and drill flow in a browser; confirm spraying, water depletion, level progression/retry, and danger mitigation work as intended.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game in Chromium at a mobile viewport and inspect the updated layout.
2. Exercise held spraying, water depletion, route safety after danger mitigation, and progression through all levels.
3. Fix any issues revealed by interactive testing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and all recent changes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Water depletion happens while spraying in the live drill; extinguishing a fire returns a small amount of water.
- Earlier browser testing covered the initial game version, but the latest changes have not been tested interactively.

## Objective
- Complete “Fire Marshal: Touch Protocol,” a playable touch-first browser game.
- Fix held spraying and water depletion, add fire types and levels, and repair the danger mitigation tool.

## Requirements
- Use HTML5 Canvas/JavaScript with touch-first controls; no keyboard or mouse required.
- Support movement, aiming, spraying, tool menus, route planning, extinguisher installation, and danger-zone mitigation.
- Render unsafe evacuation routes distinctly and expose `checkPathSafety(pathPoints, blastCircles)`.
- Latest request: “The fire fighter cant shoot at all times while the drill is started, make it shoot whenever i press shoot water, also make a bar that manages the water that can deplete, also make more levels and all the fire types so that could be extinguished, also the danger tool doesnt work, repair all these”

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation in a single `index.html` file with no framework or external dependencies.
- Water can extinguish all fire types; other equipment remains selectable.
- Progress to the next level after a successful drill; retry the current level after a failed drill.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented continuous spraying while the spray control is held during a live drill, with visible water depletion and a refill bonus for extinguishing fires.
- Added four levels with multiple fire types and per-level hazards.
- Improved danger-zone hit testing and made mitigated zones visibly distinct and safe for route checks.
- Added level, fire-count, and water-meter HUD updates; drill completion now reflects the current level’s fire count.
- `node --check /tmp/opencode/fire-marshal.js` passed after extracting the script from `index.html`.

### Active
- Test touch gameplay and drill flow in a browser; confirm spraying, water depletion, level progression/retry, and danger mitigation work as intended.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game in Chrome at a mobile viewport and inspect the layout.
2. Exercise held spraying, water depletion, route safety after danger mitigation, and progression through all levels.
3. Fix any issues revealed by interactive testing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and all recent changes.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Water depletes while spraying in the live drill; extinguishing fires returns a small amount of water.
- Earlier browser testing covered the initial game version; recent updates have not been tested interactively.

  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown

  go-back                     go back to the previous page

  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

  mouseup [button]            press mouse up

  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

## Objective
- Complete “Fire Marshal: Touch Protocol,” a playable touch-first browser game.
- Verify and fix held spraying, water depletion, fire types and levels, and danger-zone mitigation.

## Requirements
- Use HTML5 Canvas/JavaScript with touch-first controls and no external dependencies.
- Support movement, aiming, spraying, tool menus, route planning, extinguisher installation, and danger-zone mitigation.
- Render unsafe evacuation routes distinctly and expose `checkPathSafety(pathPoints, blastCircles)`.

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation in a single `index.html` file.
- Water extinguishes all fire types; other equipment remains selectable.
- Progress to the next level after a successful drill; retry the current level after failure.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented continuous spraying while the spray control is held during a live drill, a depleting water meter, and a refill bonus for extinguishing fires.
- Added four levels with multiple fire types and per-level hazards.
- Added level, fire-count, and water-meter HUD updates; drill completion reflects the current level’s fire count.
- Improved danger-zone hit testing and made mitigated zones visually distinct and ignored by route-safety checks.
- `node --check /tmp/opencode/fire-marshal.js` passed.
- Browser smoke test on a mobile viewport confirmed starting the drill and holding spray reduces water and extinguishes fire.

### Active
- Fix and verify touch selection of the danger tool and ensure mitigation works through the UI.
- Test level progression/retry and full touch gameplay in-browser.

### Blocked
